data.name: Ramanbhai
data.gender_notes: Ramanbhai is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Raman means 'Joy' in Sanskrit and Bhai means 'brother' in Hindi. Ramanbhai can be interpreted as 'Joyful Brother'. The name Ramanbhai carries the meaning “Joy in Ram” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi. Parents who choose Ramanbhai usually hope their child will grow to embody joy in ram and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Raman is a name of Lord Rama, who is considered an ideal husband, son, and king in Hinduism. Bhai refers to the bond of brotherhood and love.
data.etymology: Ramanbhai belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joy in Ram.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ramanbhai total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ramanbhai has its roots in the rich Hindu culture. Raman is a name derived from the name of Lord Rama, an avatar of Lord Vishnu, who is known for his immense joy and inner peace. The name Bhai signifies brotherhood and unity. Thus, the name Ramanbhai represents the cultural values of happiness, joy, and brotherhood.

historical_references.reference: Ramanbhai was a famous Jain scholar from Gujarat. He wrote a commentary on the Agama texts known as 'Ramabhattaraka-grantha-bhashya' in the 14th century.
Ramanbhai was also a prominent leader in the Vaishnavite Bhakti movement during the 16th century in Gujarat, and is said to have preached and popularized the devotion to Lord Rama among the masses.
